title: chore(deps): bump flutter_secure_storage from 10.2.0 to 10.3.0 in the flutter-dependencies group
body:
Bumps the flutter-dependencies group with 1 update: [flutter_secure_storage](https://github.com/mogol/flutter_secure_storage). Updates `flutter_secure_storage` from 10.2.0 to 10.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from flutter_secure_storage's releases.

v10.3.0

Android

  • Added AndroidBiometricType enum and biometricType option to AndroidOptions to control which authentication methods are accepted during biometric prompts (requires KeyCipherAlgorithm.AES_GCM_NoPadding).
    • AndroidBiometricType.biometricOrDeviceCredential (default) accepts Class 3 biometrics or device credentials (PIN/pattern/password), preserving previous behaviour.
    • AndroidBiometricType.strongBiometricOnly restricts authentication to Class 3 (strong) biometrics only; device credentials are explicitly rejected.
  • Fully enforced on Android 11+ (API 30+) via setAllowedAuthenticators on BiometricPrompt and setUserAuthenticationParameters on the KeyStore key. On earlier API levels the system may still permit device credentials.
  • Added biometricPromptNegativeButton option to AndroidOptions to customise the dismiss button label on the biometric prompt. Required when using strongBiometricOnly or on Android 10 and lower.

iOS / macOS

  • Fixed secStoreAvailabilitySink not being called when protected data availability changes.
  • Fixed kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain being added to Keychain queries unconditionally; it is now only set when useDataProtectionKeychain is explicitly enabled.

Windows

  • Fixed deleteAll and containsKey not acquiring the mutex lock, which could cause data races under concurrent access. If you are on Dart >=3.10.0, this fix is applied automatically. Otherwise, pin flutter_secure_storage_windows: ^4.2.2 in your pubspec.yaml to opt in and make sure your constraint is set for minimum of Dart >=3.10.0.

Linux

  • Fixed deleteKeyring storing the string "null" instead of an empty JSON object {}.
  • Fixed non-UTF-8 error messages from libsecret causing a FormatException on the Dart side; messages are now sanitised before being sent through the method channel.
  • Fixed locked or unavailable keyring now surfacing as a catchable PlatformException with code KeyringLocked.
  • Fixed JSON parse errors and other C++ exceptions now surfacing as a PlatformException with code StorageError instead of sending malformed bytes through the channel.

title: Support Android in integration tests
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/dd1ac80777d20141b7bd33d3f22d917f040b45872cfbc5ca53d126f3f81f30ba.jpg) `just int-test` now runs on Android. ## What changed - `_resolve-device` falls back to `adb devices` when no booted iOS simulator is found, and skips `xcrun` on hosts where it isn't installed (so Linux works too). - `int-test` auto-injects public Nostr relays through `--dart-define=WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=...` when the resolved device is an Android one. The emulator can't reach the host's localhost, so the local docker relays aren't usable there. - `integration_test/_support/app_setup.dart` reads the relay list from that dart-define (default: the same two localhost relays as before), and the TCP precheck now no-ops for non-localhost URLs. The iOS path is unchanged, and either platform can override the relay list with `WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=...`. ## Why The marmot colony hibernates near the host, but our Android sibling lives one virtual network away (it can't hear the local relays burrowing at `127.0.0.1`). So when the Android marmot wants to chat, we point it at the public relays already used in production: `nos.lol`, `relay.primal.net`, `relay.damus.io`. ## How to use ```bash # iOS simulator (unchanged) just int-test # Android emulator (auto-detected, auto-uses public relays) just int-test # Override relays on any platform WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=wss://my.relay just int-test ``` --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * Integration tests accept a comma-separated relay env var (trimmed, empty entries dropped) and pass it into test runs. * Local relay preflight parses each relay URL, validates only localhost/127.0.0.1 hosts for connectivity, and derives the port from the URL or scheme. * Device resolution now detects both booted iOS simulators and connected Android devices; test runs adapt accordingly. * **Chores** * Android test flow adds automatic port forwarding for Android devices when needed and enables debug build network config to allow cleartext to localhost. title: fix(mentions): use accent Color/500 so mentions stay legible on both bubbles
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/12fc74d461a4b879e9a68324e78d2076bf39151b9536cf557f51dcd8ad1c79f6.png) Mentions disappear on the "wrong-side" bubble in each theme. In dark mode an orange username sits at orange-50 (near-white) on a white outgoing bubble. Vlad caught it and posted the spec. The mention renderer was reading `AvatarColorSet.content`, wired to `accent.contentPrimary`. That step is `Color/900` in light mode and `Color/50` in dark, so it inverts with the theme and clashes with whichever bubble is the opposite shade. That token belongs on the tinted avatar pill, not the chat bubble. Per the foundations file (node 297-1992), mentions should use `Accent/{color}/Content Secondary`, which is `Color/500` in both modes. The 500 step is mid-saturation and reads on both white and near-black bubbles. ### Changes - `lib/utils/avatar_color.dart`: add `contentSecondary` to `AvatarColorSet`. Wires to `accent.contentSecondary` for accent buckets and `fillContentTertiary` for the neutral bucket. - `lib/widgets/markdown_text.dart`: npub mention text uses `.contentSecondary`. - `test/widgets/markdown_text_test.dart`: widget test asserts the mention color equals `contentSecondary` and is not `content`. Regression guard so a future marmot does not revert it by accident. ### Scope Mentions only. Sender names and reply-author labels have the same root cause but are outside Vlad's note. The new field is in place if we apply the rule to them later. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Style** * Updated visual styling of mentions to use improved secondary color variants, providing better visual distinction and consistency across the interface. * **Tests** * Enhanced test coverage to verify mention color styling behavior. title: fix: reset Whitenoise lifecycle after deleting data
body:
## Description

Fixes the reset lifecycle after deleting all app data.

The bridge now replaces the process-global Whitenoise handle safely: it waits for in-flight bridge calls before closing the old database, clears the global instance after delete, and exposes `reinitializeWhitenoise()` so Flutter can install a fresh instance after the local wipe completes.

Flutter wraps the delete flow with a reset-pending marker. If the app is killed or interrupted during reset, startup recovery clears the local reset surface before initializing Whitenoise again. If deletion succeeds but reinitialization fails in the same process, the app routes to the fatal error flow instead of leaving the user on settings with an uninitialized Rust singleton.

This PR also keeps the start-DM stale-group guard: cached DM group IDs are validated before opening. If the cached group no longer exists in Rust/MDK state, the app falls back to creating a fresh DM instead of failing with `Group not found`.

This app-side lifecycle fix depends on the companion `whitenoise-rs` bounded-delete PR, which prevents local data deletion from hanging behind stuck scheduler/background/relay shutdown work:

https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/840

Closes #660

title: Add markdown rendering for chat messages
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/35d671f7406873029a2b8cd5e12660eb6642cb3cdbe841a429ae0e94f0d43bff.png)


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/813ae5ee-daef-4bdf-aec6-cd0f390a2198



> Heads up: most of the diff is FRB codegen. Net total is ~7800 added lines; ~4300 of that is autogenerated `lib/src/rust/` and `rust/src/frb_generated.rs`, regenerated whenever the bridge surface changes. The hand-written review surface is ~1500 lines plus ~1700 lines of tests. Skim the codegen, read the rest.

This PR consumes the new `whitenoise_markdown::Document` AST from whitenoise-rs (pinned at `f421a8ad`). Chat bubbles now render CommonMark, GFM, and the nostr-extension format. Plain-text messages render byte-identically to before.

The marmots have learned to read bold text.

## What's in here

- `WnMarkdownText` walks the parsed AST and renders every Block and Inline variant.
- Plain-text fast path: single-paragraph messages with only Text/SoftBreak/HardBreak inlines skip the markdown renderer entirely. They keep the existing inline-timestamp layout.
- `@npub` mentions render as underlined `@DisplayName` (Vlad's design call). Tap opens a new in-app `UserProfileShade` instead of bouncing out to the OS. Non-npub Nostr URIs (note, nevent, nprofile, naddr, nrelay) still route externally because they point at events, not people.
- `SoftBreak` renders as a newline. The CommonMark default is a space, which loses every Enter press in the composer.
- URL scheme allow-list: `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `nostr`, `tel`. Anything else gets no tap recognizer at the renderer layer; the bubble's tap handler reapplies the same check before `launchUrl`. The Rust parser does not recognize HTML, so `<script>` and similar pass through as literal text.
- Surface boundaries: chat-list previews, reply quotes, notifications, and the composer keep their existing plain-text rendering.

## Bridge style

The bridge mirrors each AST type through FRB. The AST is FRB-friendly: owned `String`, `Vec<Enum>` recursion, `Clone`, `Eq`. Generated Dart sealed classes give exhaustive switch and IDE help. A hand-rolled Dart JSON parser would be a second markdown implementation and would drift from upstream.

## Tests + manual QA

- 4498 Flutter tests + 75 Rust tests pass. Coverage 99.03%. `just precommit` clean.
- Manual checklist run locally: every Block and Inline variant, surface boundaries, security cases (`javascript:`, `data:`, raw HTML stay inert), nested containers, CJK and RTL mixed runs, mention-tap into shade and back without scroll jump, long-press preview shows resolved names.

## Known limitations

1. Cross-inline highlight matches are not highlighted in search results.
2. Math renders as italic monospace source; no LaTeX engine is used.
3. Inline markdown images render as `[image: alt]` text links, not embedded.
4. Mentions of users outside the chat's metadata cache fall back to truncated npub until metadata loads. Follow-up could subscribe to mentioned pubkeys.

## Incidental upstream commits

The rev bump pulled in two non-markdown commits: `917ad14` (handle_contact_list lock contention) and `585d31f` (MDK update + push-token gossip). Both required adding `disappearing_message_secs: None` to two struct literals in `rust/src/api/groups.rs`.

body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/78dc0ac6367f959479dea509953a057bf83f10b1d64cbb0307e7f2dd507e5a91.jpg)

## What changed

`whitenoise-rs` is now pinned to the `arch-refactor` branch (sha `eefe3fe9...`). That branch removed `Whitenoise::get_instance()` and split the god object into one `AccountSession` per account.

## Shim layer

`rust/src/api/mod.rs` holds a private `tokio::sync::OnceCell<Arc<Whitenoise>>` populated by `initialize_whitenoise`. Two helpers:

- `wn() -> &'static Whitenoise` for the few global calls that remain (login, all-accounts, app settings).
- `wn_session(&pubkey) -> Arc<AccountSession>` for everything else.

Init goes through `OnceCell::get_or_try_init`, so two concurrent `initialize_whitenoise` calls share one underlying `Whitenoise::ensure_initialized` run.

## Call-site migration

About 95 sites in `rust/src/api/` moved off the deleted facades onto `session.<ops>()`:

- `session.membership().for_group(&gid)` for accept / decline / archive / unarchive / mute / unmute / pin / mark-read / clear-chat.
- `session.groups()` for visible / by-id / members / admins / create / add-members / remove-members / leave / update-data.
- `session.groups().media()` for upload / download / image-path.
- `session.drafts()`, `session.chat_list()`, `session.mute_list()`, `session.social()`, `session.key_packages()`, `session.push()`, `session.settings()`.

`get_chat_summary` now searches both active and archived chat lists so archived chats render correctly (master commit 8135cbe's intent, under the new API).

## Other adjustments

- `MuteListEntry.account_pubkey` is gone upstream; the shim now passes the pubkey through `MuteListEntry::from_entry`.
- `account.relays(...)` and `user.key_package_*(...)` now take `&Arc<SharedServices>`; the shim passes `&whitenoise.shared`.
- `AccountGroup::get` is gone; the shim uses `session.membership().for_group(&gid).get_or_create(None)`.
- The new `subscribe_to_group_state` from master switched from `Whitenoise::get_instance()` to `wn()`.

## Status

Bridge regenerated. `just precommit` is green. The colony of marmots can stop fetching from the one big burrow and head to their own.

title: fix(android): external signer notification recovery
body: ## Upstream Dependency Resolved: marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#811 has merged, and this PR points at the merged `whitenoise-rs` master revision `49e5f20c43fd72f1d07ea3675350754650955371`. ## Summary - Fix Android background notifications for multi-account external-signer users after reboot / headless foreground-service startup. - Reconcile external signer callbacks from both the UI isolate and foreground-task isolate so every persisted external-signer account has a live callback before notification handling begins. - Register external signer callbacks before ensuring Rust relay subscriptions and before attaching the headless notification stream. - Register app-local Android plugins with the headless foreground-task Flutter engine so the Android signer method channel is available outside `MainActivity`. - Keep headless notification subscriptions from requesting notification permission when no Activity is attached. - Keep the foreground service configured with the `dataSync` service type without restarting an already-running service on every cold start. - Make external signer reconciliation best-effort for non-active accounts while preserving fast-fail behavior for the activating account. ## Review Follow-up - Renamed the lifecycle helper from `ExternalSignerRegistrationService` to `ExternalSignerCallbackRegistry` to make the split from `AndroidSignerService` clearer. - Added Android platform guards in both the callback registry and `AndroidSignerService.registerExternalSigner`. - Removed the short-pubkey logging helper that implied invalid pubkeys were expected. - Removed the `@visibleForTesting` entry point from `NotificationTaskHandler`; tests now exercise retry behavior through task start/repeat/coordination events. - Removed the process-local foreground-service restart flag that would stop/start a running service on every cold start. - Collapsed foreground-task subscription tracking to the subscription source of truth, and clear `NotificationSubscription.isRunning` when the stream closes. - Left the local-account concern as code-is: reconciliation filters `AccountType.external_` before registration, and mixed local/external account tests cover that path. ## Root Cause The boot/reboot foreground task was alive and subscribed to the Rust notification stream, but it did not have external-signer callbacks registered in that headless Dart isolate. Incoming events for Amber-backed accounts could arrive and be persisted, but Rust could not fully process/decrypt them into notification updates until the main app isolate opened and `authProvider` registered the signer callbacks. The desired runtime state is now reconciled in both isolates: every signed-in external-signer account has a registered signer callback in the current process/isolate before notification handling begins. ## Manual Verification Verified on a Pixel 7 Pro with two Amber-backed accounts and a second Android sender device: - Rebooted the Amber device. - Waited for the silent `White Noise connected to relays` foreground notification. - Sent messages to both Amber-backed accounts before opening White Noise. - Both Android notifications appeared while the app remained unopened. - Logs showed the expected order: system foreground task start, external signer callback registration for both accounts, Rust relay subscription ensure, notification stream subscription, received notification updates, displayed notifications. ## Testing - `flutter test --reporter compact test/services/android_signer_service_test.dart test/services/external_signer_callback_registry_test.dart test/services/foreground_service_test.dart test/providers/auth_provider_test.dart` - `just test-flutter-quiet` - `just precommit` - Earlier Android validation: `just when-apk` plus install/manual reboot testing on physical devices. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit ## Release Notes * **New Features** * External signer callback registration is now automatically triggered when the app resumes. * **Improvements** * Enhanced external signer account reconciliation across login, logout, and profile-switching flows. * Notification permission requests are now optional and configurable. * Improved Android foreground service lifecycle handling and coordination. * **Tests** * Expanded test coverage for external signer registration, app lifecycle, and notification handling.

title: fix(android): enable boot auto-restart for foreground service
body:
## Summary

Restore notification delivery after device reboot and after app updates. The original fix (re-enable the plugin's boot/package-replaced receivers + set the Dart auto-run flags) turned out to be necessary but not sufficient — the foreground service restarted post-reboot but ran an empty task handler, so messages still didn't surface as notifications until the user reopened the app. This PR closes that loop:

- **Boot/upgrade auto-restart**: re-enabled the plugin's `RebootReceiver` / `RestartReceiver` and set `autoRunOnBoot: true` + `autoRunOnMyPackageReplaced: true`.
- **Process-scoped JNI context**: new `WhitenoiseApplication` runs `Keyring.initializeNdkContext()` in `Application.onCreate`, so Rust has the Android Context regardless of which component (Activity / Service / Receiver) starts the process.
- **Headless work in the task isolate**: extracted `NotificationSubscription` from `notificationListenerProvider` so it can run independent of the widget tree. New `_NotificationTaskHandler` bootstraps Rust + reads locale from persisted state, and on `starter=system` (boot/package-replaced) starts its own subscription.
- **Cross-isolate coordination**: main isolate sends `main_started` / `main_stopped` via `FlutterForegroundTask.sendDataToTask` so exactly one isolate owns the notification channel at a time.
- **Pending-tap handoff**: a notification fired from the task isolate persists its payload via `FlutterForegroundTask.saveData`; the main isolate consumes it on launch / resume and routes to the right chat (switching the active account first if needed).

Fixes #488.

## Why

Currently, after a device reboot the foreground service does not auto-restart, so notifications silently stop working until the user opens the app. Two stacked misconfigurations caused this:

**1. Receivers were disabled in the manifest.** [c3b4a1909](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/commit/c3b4a1909) added `android:enabled="false"` + `tools:node="replace"` as defense-in-depth against an upgrade-path crash. The *actual* root cause of that crash — `foregroundServiceType 0x201` persisted in native `SharedPreferences` while the manifest declared only `dataSync` — was already mitigated by the one-time prefs cleanup in `MainActivity.onCreate()`. That cleanup has been shipped since 2026-02-19, so any active user has run it.

**2. The Dart-side flags were never set.** `ForegroundTaskOptions.autoRunOnBoot` defaults to `false`. The plugin's `RebootReceiver.onReceive` reads this from persisted options and early-returns unless it's `true` — so even if the manifest disable were removed, boot restart still wouldn't happen.

Both fixes are required. The receiver is the plugin's *only* boot-restart mechanism, and it only fires when the Dart flags opt in.

## GrapheneOS impact

This is particularly important for GrapheneOS users. They typically don't run sandboxed Google Play Services, so the MIP05 FCM-based push plan won't reach them — the foreground service is their only notification path. Without boot auto-restart, every reboot silently breaks notifications until the app is manually reopened.

The receivers use pure AOSP APIs (`BOOT_COMPLETED`, `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED`, `AlarmManager`) with no GMS dependency, so they work on GrapheneOS.

## Known limitation: first install / upgrade

`autoRunOnBoot` and `autoRunOnMyPackageReplaced` are persisted by the plugin only when Dart calls `FlutterForegroundTask.init()`. On the very first install or upgrade to a build containing this PR, the previous Dart-persisted flag values are still in `SharedPreferences` (default `false`), so:

- The `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED` broadcast that fires immediately after the upgrade reads the stale `false` and skips auto-start.
- A reboot before the user has opened the new build will likewise skip auto-start.

After the user opens the app one time on this build, the new flags are persisted and every subsequent reboot or update auto-starts correctly.

A native-side workaround (seeding the plugin's `SharedPreferences` from `WhitenoiseApplication.onCreate`) would close this one-time gap, but it couples our code to plugin-internal pref schema — the same layer that produced the `0x201` bitmask incident in [c3b4a1909](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/commit/c3b4a1909). Deferring with documentation is the safer trade for a one-time UX hiccup.

## Residual risk

A user who hasn't launched the app since before 2026-02-19 could still have stale `0x201` in their prefs. On next reboot, `RebootReceiver` would try to start the service with that stale type and crash. Likelihood is low (2+ months of launches since the cleanup shipped), but non-zero. The `MainActivity.onCreate()` cleanup stays in place as a safety net on the next normal launch.

## Android 15 note

If `targetSdk` is ever bumped to 35+, the OS itself blocks boot-launched `dataSync` foreground services regardless of plugin setup. At that point the service type needs to change (likely to `remoteMessaging` or `specialUse`). Not blocking today; worth flagging for when the SDK bump happens.

## Test plan

- [x] `just precommit` passes (formatting, linting, Flutter + Rust tests, 99.36% coverage)
- [x] Spike confirmed on a real device that the task isolate can reach Rust, platform channels, and persisted accounts on a freshly rebooted process (`starter=system` path)
- [x] Spike confirmed `flutter_local_notifications` can fire from the task isolate
- [ ] Manual: install on a Pixel, send a test message, reboot, confirm a notification appears without opening the app
- [ ] Manual: repeat on GrapheneOS (no sandboxed Play Services)
- [ ] Manual: verify the in-app/background handoff doesn't produce duplicate notifications when toggling between foreground and background while messages arrive

title: Add disappearing messages support
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/0074236e7be0ccf1467235e0f709fda9c31f977d1295cb471ea3a9540e8a17cc.jpg)

Needs: marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#730

Implements the Flutter side of disappearing messages. When an admin sets a TTL on a group, every new message stored gets an expires_at timestamp. A background task in the Rust layer sweeps expired rows every 30 seconds and notifies the UI.

## What changed

**Rust API layer** (rust/src/api/): Added expires_at field to ChatMessage, two new functions (set_disappearing_messages, get_disappearing_message_duration), bumped whitenoise-rs and mdk-core dependencies to pick up the disappearing messages support.

**Hook** (lib/hooks/use_disappearing_messages.dart): Manages loading and setting the disappearing message duration per group. Exposes current duration, loading/saving states, and error handling.

**Group info screen**: Admins see a dropdown selector (Off / 30s / 5min / 1hr / 1day / 1week) to configure the disappearing message timer for the group.

**Message bubbles**: Messages with an expiration timestamp display a small timer icon next to the timestamp, so users know the message will disappear.

**L10n**: Added 12 new localization keys across all 8 locale files.

**Tests**: 58 new tests covering the format utility (24), the hook (19), the bubble ephemeral indicator (7), and the group info screen dropdown (8). All 4009 Flutter tests and 42 Rust tests pass. Precommit green.

## Design decisions

- **Dedicated API functions over FlutterGroupDataUpdate**: flutter_rust_bridge doesn't support Option<Option<T>>, so set/get disappearing messages use standalone functions, which gives a cleaner separation of concerns.
- **No retroactive expiry**: Changing the duration only affects new messages, matching the Rust layer's approach and Signal/WhatsApp behavior.
- **Timer icon, not countdown**: The bubble shows a static timer icon to indicate the message is ephemeral, while the Rust layer handles actual cleanup on its 30-second sweep cycle.

This marmot built hourglasses into the message bubbles. When your time is up, poof.
